blocks.prompt: 10 A spacecraft moves from point \((120, 240, -50)\) to point \((130, 210, 80)\) in kilometers. What is the magnitude of the displacement vector in kilometers?
blocks.explanation:
Displacement is the vector from the start point to the end point.
We must find its length in kilometres.
Plan: end minus start for each coordinate, then the magnitude formula (this is the distance formula).
steps:
Given: start \(P(120, 240, -50)\), end \(Q(130, 210, 80)\), in km.
To find: \(|\overrightarrow{PQ}|\).
Method: \(\overrightarrow{PQ} = (x_2 - x_1)\underline{i} + (y_2 - y_1)\underline{j} + (z_2 - z_1)\underline{k}\), then its magnitude.

Displacement vector
\[\overrightarrow{PQ} = (130 - 120)\underline{i} + (210 - 240)\underline{j}\]
\[\quad + (80 - (-50))\underline{k}\]
\[= 10\underline{i} - 30\underline{j} + 130\underline{k}\]
Why: End coordinates minus start coordinates.

Simplify
\[\sqrt{17900} = \sqrt{100 \times 179}\]
\[= 10\sqrt{179} \approx 133.8\]
Why: 100 is a perfect square factor; 179 is prime.

Check (size)
\[130 < 133.8 < 10 + 30 + 130\]
Why: The length must be at least the largest component (130) and at most the sum of the component sizes (170).
